Test Latin substitution on Takahashi with glyph order reversed within words at the published noisy-control search budget.
Test the fixed glyph-substitution layer of Caspari and Faccini's proposed Italian shorthand key.
Among nine public-practice Latin substitution searches, Takahashi with reversed word order gave the highest compression savings (−11.122% versus −11.442% for the previous key), at the per-view budget
Catalogue Rozanova and Temerev's controlled tests of Voynich glyphs, tokens and separators.

Test Vlegels’s published Italian token map and deterministic prefix rules.

Register Hauer and Kondrak’s synthetic benchmarks and their open questions about transposition and transcription noise.
A mixture of vocabulary, habit chain, near-copying, templates, line position and a glyph-trigram speller predicts held-out words better than a bag of words.
